Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

stareal (development version)

2026-10-26: percent, panel labels, progress

  • Prevalence is in percent (0 to 100) everywhere: predict()’s summaries and kept draws, plot(), crossval()’s observed and predicted prevalences (and so its RMSE, in percentage points), simulate_areal()’s true prevalence, and summary(fit, latent = TRUE). Exceedance thresholds are given in percent too: exceedance = 5 reports p_gt_5, the probability (0 to 1) that prevalence exceeds 5%.
  • Panel labels. plot(pr, ids = , labels = ) titles time-series panels with your own labels, one per id or named by id.
  • Progress from predict(). It reports the draws conditioned and predicted so far, with an estimate of the time left, in both phases and from parallel workers too.

2026-10-25: example data and the website

  • Example data. igad_crt76t holds 328 surveys of the chloroquine-resistance marker crt K76T in the eight IGAD countries, from the public STAVE collation. The surveys were selected by location, not by STAVE’s country names, which are unreliable. No boundaries ship with the package: the examples and tutorials download GADM with geodata::gadm().
  • Plots. plot(fit) shows every parameter of summary(), fixed effects included. Time-series plots of predictions (plot(pr), by area or group) add the observed prevalence of each surveyed area and time step, with its exact 95% binomial interval (data = TRUE).
  • Title. “Spatial-Temporal Areal Estimation from Survey Data”.
  • Borders that nearly touch. areal_frame(adjacency_snap = ) makes units whose borders come within that many metres neighbours. This is for boundary files assembled from different sources, which leave small gaps along national borders.
  • Folds of your own. crossval(folds = ) takes a fold label per observed cell, e.g. a country, for spatial cross-validation.
  • Comparing models. compare_cv() compares models cross-validated on the same folds, cell by cell, with the standard error of the difference.
  • Simulating at a real design. simulate_areal(cells = ) surveys the given area-time cells, with their numbers tested, so a simulation can copy a real survey design.
  • Fix: cross-validation log scores. The quadrature behind crossval()’s log score found the integrand’s mode by plain Newton steps. When a held-out survey was far from its predictive mean, these overshot, and the log score came out wrong by thousands (e.g. -18,698 for a survey inside its 95% interval). The steps are now damped. PIT, intervals and RMSE were not affected.
  • Website. Five tutorials (crt K76T by month, k13 R561H in East Africa, covariates, cross-validation, simulation), each running in minutes. The two long computations, the cross-validation of five models and a 20-replicate simulation study, ship with the package in inst/extdata/ and are imported by their tutorials.

2026-10-25: review and restructure

Interface

  • Simulations. simulate_areal() returns data ready to fit (a stareal_data with $truth), so fit_areal(sim) works directly.
  • Fit arguments. fit_areal(data, formula = ~ trend() + x, ...): formula replaces mean, and checkpoint_dir is now an argument of fit_areal() and crossval(). priors and control accept plain lists of just the settings to change, and fixed-effect priors can be named by design column.
  • Settings. areal_priors() and mcmc_control() return plain validated lists. In mcmc_control(), n_cores = 1 replaces parallel = FALSE, and verbose replaces progress.
  • Summaries. summary() and diagnose() return one class. diagnose() adds every observed cell, a check of the fixed effects’ ESS, and the verdict.
  • Prediction. predict(fit, groups = ...) replaces levels, and group tables are now under pr$groups. New: as.data.frame(pr) and sf::st_as_sf(pr, time = ...).
  • Draws. All posterior::as_draws_*() conversions work on a fit.
  • Time. time_frame(n_steps = ) replaces T, and its field is $n_steps. trend() runs from -1 at the first time step to 1 at the last, and is dropped when there is one step.
  • areal_data() no longer prints on assignment, and its surveys carry .id (the area id).

Sampler

  • The pseudo-data that steer the latent and hyperparameter moves are refitted at the chain’s mean during burn-in, then frozen. For rare outcomes this mixes the latent cells about 8 times better.
  • Chains start from dispersed points, so R-hat can reveal chains that have not mixed.
  • Seeds:
    • each chain and each prediction draw gets its own seed, drawn from the user’s, so any seed works;
    • results do not depend on the session’s RNGkind().

Running

  • Live progress. Worker processes’ progress now appears in RStudio, not only in a terminal.
  • Interrupts. On interrupt or error, the workers are stopped instead of running on.
  • Checkpoint folders. A folder is tied to its data, graph, model, settings and sampler version, but not to the R version.

Cross-validation

  • The log score integrates the held-out Gaussian exactly.
  • “Outside the 95% interval” uses a randomised PIT, so a calibrated model shows about 5% whatever the number tested.

Fixes

About 80 smaller fixes: input validation (factors, date-times, numeric ids, non-finite values, name clashes), memory bounds in prediction, messages, and documentation. See review_stareal-v0.1_2026-10-24.md in the source repository.
